For a reversible adiabatic process, $PV^\gamma=$ constant and the work done by the gas is $W=\dfrac{P_1V_1-P_2V_2}{\gamma-1}$.
Find $\gamma$: $\gamma=\dfrac{c_p}{c_v}=\dfrac{3R}{2R}=1.5$.
Initial state: $P_1V_1=8\times10^5\,\text{Pa}\times0.15\,\text{m}^3=1.2\times10^5\,\text{J}$.
Final volume: $V_2=V_1\left(\dfrac{P_1}{P_2}\right)^{1/\gamma}=0.15\times8^{2/3}\,\text{m}^3=0.6\,\text{m}^3$.
Final state: $P_2V_2=10^5\,\text{Pa}\times0.6\,\text{m}^3=0.6\times10^5\,\text{J}$.
Work done: $W=\dfrac{1.2\times10^5-0.6\times10^5}{0.5}\,\text{J}=1.2\times10^5\,\text{J}=120\,\text{kJ}$.
The temperature of 140°C is not needed, because $P_1V_1$ is known directly.
Answer: 120
